t3.text: 3 · The screens behind each card, and the Library bridge

s1a.text:
THE NATIVE SEARCH STAYS EXACTLY AS IT IS
RootView keeps .searchable on the TabView with .tabViewSearchActivation(.searchTabSelection). The field, its place at the bottom and the tab-bar morph are not touched. Only the idle content of SearchScreen changes: while the query is empty and the field is not focused, the same ScrollView that shows results today shows the three plates.
STATES
• Idle: the plates.
• Field focused, nothing typed: the plates cross-fade out (200 ms; Reduce Motion: no fade) and today’s Recent list or hint shows.
• Typing: today’s grouped results, unchanged.
• Clear or close: the plates return.
Dev note: focus is read with @Environment(\.isSearching) or .searchFocused on RootView; check in the simulator.

s1b.text:
METRICS
Title “Discover” / “Keşfet”: Literata 34/500, at the Library title position. The tab keeps its name, Search / Ara.
Plate: full width inside the 24 gutter, height 124, radius 16 continuous, 0.5 pt rule ring, 2 pt paper gap between strips. Short screens: height = min(124, 14 % of screen height), 95 on iPhone SE. From 600 pt of width the plates sit three across.
Label on paper, 10 under the plate: Literata 20/500 ink, then SF 13 ink2. Chevron 8 × 14 ink3. 22 between cards. No text on the images, no scrim, no glass on the cards.
The plate and its label are one button; pressed = opacity 0.85. VoiceOver: “Composers, 52 composers, button”; the images are decorative.
The scroll content ends above the field through the system safe area.

s1c.text:
FREE USERS
Browsing is open to everyone, like the Library and its filters. The plates, the lists and the era and form pages look the same for free and Premium; past pieces carry the Library lock and open the paywall, today’s piece opens.
Typing is Premium: when a free user taps the field, the screen shows today’s locked state (“Search is part of Premium”, See Premium) in place of Recent. The paywall no longer opens by itself on entering the tab.
NAVIGATION
The plates push inside the Search tab’s NavigationStack (a new router.searchPath). The glass field stays visible on pushed pages; typing there returns to the root and shows results. Pieces open through router.openPiece, as search results do today. Composer rows open the existing ComposerSheet.

s2a.text:
ERA COLLAGES: HOW THE PAINTINGS ARE PICKED
Picked by hand once and stored as piece ids (new content/eras.yaml, collage: ids). The app uses those pieces’ existing thumbs, so no new image files.
1. The painting was made in the era itself, give or take a decade. Many pairings are deliberately from another century; those are left out.
2. It belongs to a piece by a composer of that era. One exception: Renaissance has three pieces only, so Giorgione’s The Tempest (c. 1506–08) is borrowed from Vivaldi’s Summer.
3. Different painters, at least two composers, strips in date order.
4. The subject must survive a narrow vertical crop: each pick gets a focal_x (new, 0–1), like focal_y on portraits.
5. No painting appears in two eras.
The picks come from the whole 200-piece catalogue, not only from published pieces, so the cards do not change every day.

s2b.text:
FORMS: MUSIC IN PAINTINGS
The catalogue already holds paintings of people playing: Menzel’s flute concert, Danhauser’s Liszt at the piano, Mercier, Longhi, Zoffany, Lerolle. One per form, picked by hand and stored as piece ids (form_images in the same data file). All three cards then speak one visual language.
Symphonies and Orchestral works have no literal picture, so their picks are evocative.
To review: Böcklin for Violin concertos (dark).

s3a.text:
LISTS REUSE WHAT EXISTS
Composer row = LibraryRow geometry: 64 pt thumb (radius 8), SF 13 ink2 meta above, Literata 16/500 name, chevron. The thumb is the portrait, cover-cropped at focal_y. No portrait on file (Tallis, Pachelbel, Rodrigo, Barber): the stripe placeholder with the initial in Literata. A row opens the existing ComposerSheet.
Sort: the Library’s glass segmented control, A–Z (by surname) | By era (era headings, composers by birth year).
Era page: plate 124, title Literata 30, dates SF 14 ink2, one sentence in Literata 17/1.6, then Composers (a shelf of 76 pt portrait tiles, tap = ComposerSheet) and Pieces (LibraryRow; today’s piece first, then by year written).
Form page: title, count, the Library’s Composer filter chip, then LibraryRows in the same order.
Back: the 44 pt glass circle used on the piece page.
LIBRARY BRIDGE
Era and form pages end with a row “Show in Library” / “Kitaplık’ta göster” (SF 17 accent, chevron): it switches to the Library tab with that era or form filter set. In the Library, while a composer filter is selected, one accent line under the chips (“Mozart’s page” / “Mozart’ın sayfası”, SF 15, 44 pt hit area) opens the ComposerSheet. The Library is otherwise unchanged.

s3b.text:
LOCKS, AS IN THE LIBRARY
For a free user a past piece shows the lock (18 pt, ink3) where the chevron would be and opens the paywall; today’s piece shows “· Today” and opens; a birthday gift shows “· Open today” / “· Bugün açık”. Rows are never dimmed. Cards and section pages carry no lock and no badge: the lock appears only on the row of the locked piece.
WHAT IS VISIBLE
All 52 composers and all six eras are listed from the start; a piece count shows only when there is one, and an era with no piece yet shows its composers and one line. Forms appear with their first published piece (six of eleven on 28 November), with one footer line saying so. Counts are published pieces (20 on 28 November, one more each day).
NO NEW ENDPOINT
Everything comes from /v1/pieces and /v1/composers, which the app already loads. New: a small eras/forms data file (dates, descriptions, collage and form picks), bundled and served like the glossary.
